# Lab notebook {.unnumbered}

## 2026-09-09 — Program start: from the audit's agenda to preregistered experiments {#sec-nb-start}

**Setting.** The companion review of the ISLA record
(`research/cross_dataset_generalization/`, untracked; rendered report at its `_book/index.html`)
audited the repository, thirty-one primary papers and five analytic
controls, and concluded that the record does not establish a cross-dataset
accuracy advantage for ISLA; with the freestream input matched, GeoTransolver
and Transolver are more accurate at both completed HiLiftAeroML rungs, and on
the DrivAerML → SHIFT-SUV fastback transfer ISLA's source-only error is 0.99
against GeoTransolver's 0.59, both falling to 0.11–0.13 when the estate family
joins training. The review proposed four directions (rich computational
support with independent queries; topology- and conditioning-aware boundary
responses; local flux responses with numerical global coupling; transferred
correction spaces), a physical-input prerequisite, and a nonlinear extension.

**Decision.** This program runs in a worktree parallel to the main ISLA
session (which owns the program book and its cluster lanes) and keeps in
sync with it at milestones. Order of work, as the review recommended:
controls first (C1 pressure-offset versus spatial error, eval-only on saved
predictions; C2 source-only normalization audit; C3 a paired
physical-condition control with exact labels), then in parallel the
computational-support study (D1, which needs training lanes and therefore
node budget from the main program) and the three nonlearned gates (D2
boundary-response rank and basis transfer on 2D Laplace; D3 local-response
composition on 2D diffusion ports; D4 solver correction-space transfer on 2D
finite-element systems), each run by a separate agent in its own worktree
with a preregistration written before its first run. A literature chapter
(L) asks what classical solvers do that surrogates do not.

**Heilmeier answers, compressed.** We want field and force predictions on
geometries and families outside the training distribution without a new
labeled dataset. Today's surrogates fit their family and fail outside it,
and the largest reported advantages in this program turned out to be
protocol artifacts. The new element is not an architecture but a set of
gates: each proposed mechanism has a cheap nonlearned test that can reject
it before training. If it works, the payoff is a surrogate whose failure
modes are understood and whose accuracy is stated with its cost. The risks
are that no mechanism passes its gate (a useful negative), or that a passing
gate does not carry to turbulent 3D data. Cost: CPU studies today; one
four-lane training study when budget allows.

## 2026-09-09 — Preregistered: C1, pressure-offset versus spatial error on the fastback transfer {#sec-nb-c1-prereg}

**Setting.** DrivAerML (static wheels, fixed freestream, OpenFOAM hybrid
RANS–LES) and SHIFT-SUV (rolling floor, rotating wheels, a different
freestream speed and a different detached-eddy formulation) are different
label-generating conventions on smooth single-body car families. Pressure is
nondimensionalized by each dataset's own metadata (q_∞) and not shifted, so
a difference in the two datasets' pressure reference would appear in a
zero-shot prediction as a per-case constant, and a constant is exactly what
makes a relative L2 error approach 1.0 when the predicted field is otherwise
sensible. ISLA's source-only fastback error is 0.99; GeoTransolver's 0.59.

**Instrument (eval-only).** From the saved zero-shot predictions
(`smoke_fastback/{mt2_v3c,gt_fixed,mt2_multi,gt_multi}_seed{42,43,44}`, 99
fastback cases) and the in-family DrivAerML evaluations of the same
checkpoints, with cell areas recomputed from the saved triangles and cell
normals from the saved mesh: per case and arm (seed-mean predictions), the
area-weighted mean error (the offset), the centered remainder, the share of
area-weighted squared error carried by the offset, the relative L2 error of
the full and of the offset-removed error against the centered true field,
the surface closedness |Σ a n| / Σ a, and the relative error of the
integrated pressure force with and without the offset. Script:
`studies/controls/pressure_offset_diagnostic.py`.

**Bars, in readout units.** For the two source-only fastback arms:
*offset-dominated* if the constant carries ≥ 50% of the area-weighted
squared error (median over cases) and the offset-removed relative L2 is at
most 0.6 of the full one; *spatial* if the constant carries ≤ 20%; between,
mixed. The in-family arms must show an offset share ≤ 10%, or the instrument
is not measuring a transfer effect. Force: on surfaces with closedness
≤ 0.05 the force error with and without the offset must agree within the
offset's share, or the normals are inconsistent and the force reading is
withdrawn.

**What each outcome changes.** Offset-dominated: the historical transfer
gap is a label-convention question before it is an architecture question;
C3 (paired physical conditions) becomes the next control, and any transfer
claim must state the pressure reference. Spatial: the gap is a genuine field
error; the offset hypothesis is closed and D1/D2 proceed on their own
merits. Either way the readout is descriptive: target labels are used only
to diagnose, never to correct predictions.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: C1 spatial — the zero-shot fastback error is a field error, not a pressure-reference offset (offset share 1.5–2.6% for ISLA, 3.0–3.2% for GeoTransolver) {#sec-nb-c1-verdict}

**Readout** (@sec-nb-c1-prereg; `studies/controls/pressure_offset_2026-09-09.json`;
99 fastback cases, 48 DrivAerML validation cars; seed-mean predictions;
the GeoTransolver source-only and in-family arms use seeds 45 and 46 because
the seed 42–44 predictions of the historical reduction are no longer on
disk, the configuration being identical). Relative errors are on gauge
pressure about the area-weighted case mean, so their scale differs from the
program book's standardized metric; ratios between arms agree with it.

| arm | seeds | rel. L2 (full error) | rel. L2 (offset removed) | offset share of area-weighted squared error | offset ÷ true RMS | force rel. error | force rel. error, offset removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, DrivAerML only → fastback | 3 | 1.015 | 1.019 | 1.5% | +0.135 | 1.63 | 1.64 |
| GeoTransolver, DrivAerML only → fastback | 2 | 0.786 | 0.785 | 3.0% | +0.134 | 1.39 | 1.39 |
| ISLA, + estate → fastback | 3 | 0.121 | 0.121 | 0.8% | -0.014 | 0.28 | 0.28 |
| GeoTransolver, + estate → fastback | 3 | 0.101 | 0.101 | 0.2% | -0.004 | 0.20 | 0.20 |
| ISLA, DrivAerML in-family | 3 | 0.093 | 0.093 | 0.4% | +0.000 | 0.04 | 0.04 |
| GeoTransolver, DrivAerML in-family | 2 | 0.085 | 0.085 | 0.2% | -0.000 | 0.04 | 0.04 |

: Surface closedness |Σ a n| / Σ a is 0.024 on the fastback meshes and 0.022
on DrivAerML, so the pressure-force integral is well defined and a constant
offset cannot move it by more than 2.4% of its magnitude; the force columns
agree to that accuracy.

**Verdict: spatial, for both architectures.** The constant carries 1.5%
(ISLA) and 3.0% (GeoTransolver) of the source-only squared error by the
median over cases (2.6% and 3.2% by the mean), far below the 20% floor of the
"spatial" band; removing it changes the relative error by under 1%. The in-family arms pass the instrument check (offset share
under 1%). The offsets that do exist are small and of the same sign for
both models (+0.14 of the true field's RMS), which is consistent with a
modest difference of pressure reference between the datasets but explains
none of the gap. The transfer failure is a spatial field error, and it is
also a force error: 1.6x (ISLA) and 1.4x (GeoTransolver) of the true force
magnitude against 0.04 in-family, falling to 0.28 and 0.20 when the estate
family joins training.

**What it changes.** The pressure-reference hypothesis is closed. The
compound physical-condition mismatch between the datasets (ground and wheel
motion, freestream speed, solver formulation) remains the leading
explanation that is not about architecture, and C3 tests its logic on an
exactly specified problem. Any transfer claim in this program states the
force error alongside the field error, since a field error of 0.9 is a force
error above 100%.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D4 stops — a free geometric coarse grid beats a frozen source-fitted correction space on every held-out elliptic system {#sec-nb-d4-verdict}

The solver-space probe (`studies/solver_spaces/`, preregistered in its
`PREREG.md` before the run, 47 s on one CPU) compared a frozen proper
orthogonal decomposition of smoother-resistant source errors against
equal-dimension classical coarse spaces on 2D finite-element diffusion
systems with holes, under within-family, topology and coefficient shifts.
The frozen space left 0.75–0.96 of the slow-mode error where the geometric
coarse grid left 0.47–0.73 (ratios 0.62–0.76 against bars of 2.0 and 1.5),
and complete solves with it cost 19–72% *more* work than with the classical
space; the per-target oracle decomposition lost to the grid as well. The
mechanism is that solution snapshots span the right-hand sides seen at the
source geometries, not the operator's slow subspace, which for an elliptic
operator under a point smoother is generic smoothness and comes free. The
convection–diffusion variant was uninformative at mesh Péclet 0.5 and is
recorded as not measured. Chapter @sec-solver-spaces has the tables; the
direction's only remaining homes are operator classes where classical
coarse spaces fail, and learned smoothers or prolongations on a classical
hierarchy, both behind prerequisite gates (@sec-classical-solvers).

## 2026-09-09 — C2, source-only normalization: audited from the configurations, one item flagged {#sec-nb-c2-verdict}

Both transfer dataset configurations (`drivaer_ml_surface.yaml`,
`shift_suv_fastback_surface.yaml`) nondimensionalize pressure and wall shear
by each case's own metadata (dynamic pressure) with no shift, and normalize
wall shear by a declared per-dataset constant (standard deviation 0.00313
for DrivAerML, 0.00183 for SHIFT-SUV; zero mean). Inference denormalizes
predictions with the statistics saved at training time (source-side), and
the relative L2 metric is invariant to a common scale, so the differing wall
shear constants do not bias the reported relative errors; they would bias
any absolute or mixed-field loss. Pressure carries no normalization
constant beyond the physical nondimensionalization, so the C1 result is not
a normalization artifact either. Flagged: the wall-shear constant is
target-side in the target configuration (a statistic of SHIFT-SUV chosen
when its config was written); for a zero-shot protocol the target
configuration should carry the source's constant, which changes nothing
for relative metrics and is recorded here as a protocol rule. Verdict:
normalizations are source-only in effect for the reported metrics; one
declared-constant hygiene item.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D3 not worth a learner as proposed — smooth-mode local errors are amplified 4–30x by the interface solve and grids grow superlinearly; the surviving form is a hybrid with exact low modes {#sec-nb-d3-verdict}

The composition gate (`studies/composition/`, preregistered in its
`PREREG.md`, 1,064 s on one CPU) assembled 2D finite-element diffusion
components with identical straight ports into chains and grids of 2–16
components and perturbed every local response by a relative Frobenius error
ε. Exact composition is exact (composition law 2 × 10⁻¹⁶, interface solve
5 × 10⁻¹⁵). At ε = 10⁻² the median global energy error is 1.7% for two
components, 7% for chains of eight, 33% for grids of eight and 34% for grids
of sixteen (a 6.2x growth from four to sixteen, faster than linear), missing
the 5% bar; errors concentrated on rough port modes are damped 20–100x while
errors on smooth modes are amplified 4–30x and set the global error, since
the smooth small-eigenvalue part of a response carries the load (truncating
a response below 63 of 64 modes fails catastrophically). Transfer-optimal
port modes transfer to new shapes but need 13–15 of 15 modes for 1%;
proper-orthogonal modes are shape-specific; at rank 4 both leave 16–27%
error, missing the reduction bar. The interface solve is cheaper than the
monolithic solve only up to four components, and a partition-of-unity coarse
space does not help the iteration count. The narrow-channel family did not
place a barrier at a port, so the near-field claim is untested by this
instrument. Verdict against the bars: not worth a learner as proposed. What
survives is a hybrid solver (exact smooth low-mode response, learned rough
remainder), with a split-response test and a port-adjacent barrier family as
its next nonlearned gates, not launched here. Chapter @sec-composition has
the tables; figures `studies/composition/fig_*.png`.

## 2026-09-09 — D1 launched: six lanes for computational support with a depth-matched passive readout {#sec-nb-d1-launch}

**What was built** (merged from the D1 track, commit 834bd779e on this
branch). `ISLA(support_tokens=True, query_independent=True,
n_query_scalars=1, query_mass="source_total", n_decoder_layers=K)`: the
forward takes `support_points / support_normals / support_scalars`, which
join the encoder as interacting tokens with the same invariant seeds, a
token-type offset and a learned total mass equal to a learned fraction of
the total source measure; requested `query_points / query_normals /
query_scalars` are decoded passively through K read blocks that see the
final slice states, the anchors and a normalized log-space kernel readout of
all encoder tokens. Ten contract tests pass (exact query independence with
the support fixed, at 1e-12, alone or with 500 foreign companions; SE(3)
covariance; drive degree one; measure-scale and source-refinement
invariance; gauge scale equivariance; geo_checkpoint exactness; every
parameter receives gradients); the existing ISLA suites (63) pass. Recipe:
a `SplitInteriorSupport` transform moves the first `n_support` interior
points of the reader's deterministic per-case sample into a
`boundaries.support` mesh carrying the signed distance and its gradient;
dataset `drivaer_ml_volume_support.yaml` (10,000 vehicle cells by
`boundary_subsample: cells`, 10,000 interior points split 5,000 support +
5,000 queries); model `isla_volume_support.yaml`.

**Lanes** (jobs 691276–691281, names v0sup-0..5, launcher
v0/v0_support_aga.sbatch, code snapshot `code_support`, recipe copy
`recipe_support` so the program's frozen recipe is untouched; frozen V0
protocol, unit-direction drive, 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, bf16, seeds 42/43):
SUPPORT-12 (`v0_isla_support12_seed{42,43}`), PASSIVE-12
(`v0_isla_passive12_seed{42,43}`: no support tokens, 12 read blocks with the
SDF scalar) and SUPPORT-4 (`v0_isla_support4_seed{42,43}`). Node budget
confirmed by the main session (25 → 31 of 32 program nodes). Two cluster
conventions were reconciled before submission and are recorded here: the
frozen recipe's model configs carry `# @package _global_` (added to the
repository yaml too) and address surface tokens as
`boundaries.vehicle.cell_normals` / `cell_areas`, so the cluster copy of the
model yaml uses those keys while the repository yaml keeps the nested
`cell_data.*` keys of the upstream-merged recipe; model overrides are
`model.<kwarg>`.

**References and bars** (PREREG.md, written before launch). The support
arms read 10,000 vehicle cells, so their primary reference is the QT+SDF arm
at 10,000 cells (0.0572 / 0.0848 / 0.1187), with the ~365-cell arm
(0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215) reported alongside since V0-SURF10K showed the two
differ by under 3%. Supported if SUPPORT-12 is within 3% of the reference on
all three fields (≤ 0.0584 / 0.0879 / 0.1251 against the 365-cell numbers as
preregistered; ≤ 0.0589 / 0.0873 / 0.1223 against the 10k-cell numbers,
both reported) and the sentinel error is independent of the companion count
within the bf16 floor measured on the legacy passive checkpoint; falsified
if pressure ≥ 0.0624; between, the SUPPORT-4 and PASSIVE-12 arms decompose
depth against interaction.

## 2026-09-09 — Finding while building D1: the legacy passive kernel readout clamps the kernel mass, so far-from-surface queries scale with the absolute source weights {#sec-nb-passive-clamp}

In `physicsnemo/experimental/nn/isla/model.py`, the passive decoder's local
token readout `_kernel_readout(q_r, src_r, src_h, src_w, rho, eps)` (called
from `_ReadBlock.forward` when `src_h` is given, with
`rho = local_readout_rho`, default 0.02 in gauge-normalized coordinates)
computes `k = exp(-d²/ρ²) · w` and divides by `mass = k.sum(-1).clamp_min(eps)`.
For a query farther than a few ρ from every source point the true mass is
below `eps = 1e-12`, the clamp replaces it, and the readout becomes
`Σ k h / eps`, which scales with the absolute source weights instead of
being a weighted mean: in the D1 track's test a 4.2x rescale of the source
weights moved the legacy passive output by 0.16 in relative norm at such
queries. With ρ = 0.02 and interior queries whose median wall distance is
about 5 mm on a 4 m car (below ρ in gauge units) most queries are inside the
kernel's reach, but the far tail of the interior sample is not, so the
legacy passive arm's 2.6x pressure deficit (program book, interior chapter)
includes a contribution from this readout regime that the arm's
measure-scale contract test did not exercise. The legacy path is left
bitwise unchanged so trained checkpoints reproduce; the support path uses an
exactly normalized log-space form (softmax over sources with logits
−d²/ρ² + log w), identical where the mass is not tiny. The PASSIVE-12 arm,
which uses the normalized readout with 12 read blocks and the SDF scalar,
bounds how much of the 2.6x was readout and depth rather than passivity;
the main session has asked for this note to attach a caveat to that figure
once the arm reports.

**Launch acceptance (addendum).** SUPPORT-12 steps at 0.52 s and 10.8 GB
per GPU and SUPPORT-4 at 0.46 s and 7.1 GB (the QT+SDF reference: 0.28 s,
6.3 GB), both at epoch 3–4 within the first hour; the cost readout is
therefore already known to be 1.6–1.9x the reference's step time. The two
PASSIVE-12 chains blocked at model construction: with `support_tokens=false`
the model rejects `query_mass=source_total` (the option needs interacting
query or support tokens), so the override `model.query_mass=geometric_mean`
was added to that arm (inert without interacting tokens), the block markers
were cleared and the chains resubmitted (jobs 691370/691371). The
preregistration is unchanged by this: the arm's definition never involved
a query mass.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D2 partial — the Laplace boundary response minus its principal part is low-rank and resolution-stable, but its basis does not transfer across topology, gaps or corners (source-fitted basis 7–80x worse than the oracle at equal rank) {#sec-nb-d2-verdict}

The boundary-response gate (`studies/boundary_response/`, preregistered in
its `PREREG.md` before any computation; 65 min of CPU under a 12 GB cap)
assembled qualified 2D Laplace Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators by a Nyström
discretization (unit-disk DtN exact to 10⁻¹³; 22 of 23 geometries converged
to 10⁻⁸ under resolution doubling; one repair before the study, a kernel
rescaling that removes the plain log kernel's singularity at unit
logarithmic capacity). Ranks for 1% Frobenius error: full operator 184–1,467
(essentially the node count); residual after the exact arclength-Fourier
principal part |k| 8–58 for ellipses, stars, two-body pairs down to gap 0.02
and rounded squares down to corner radius 0.016, and 160 of 740 for the
thinnest annulus; removing component constants changes ranks by at most 2;
the energy pairing lowers ranks 25–45%. Rank grows with narrowing gaps
roughly as (g/L)^−0.4 while the residual's share of the operator grows from
7% to 44% of the energy norm. A basis fitted on the source development set
(single bodies and wide-gap pairs), evaluated at each held-out block's
oracle rank, is 46x (gaps), 7x (annuli) and 34x (corners) worse than the
oracle in the energy pairing (medians; worst 70x, 33x, 61x), against a bar
of 2x; to reach 1% it needs ranks 30 / 78 / 50 against oracle 13 / 22 / 9.
Verdict against the bars: part one (compressibility at ≤ 1/3 of the full
rank) passes; part two (transfer within 2x of the oracle) fails by one to
two orders of magnitude → partial. What survives: a learner would have to be
a geometry-to-operator map producing a rank-r residual in component-local
coordinates with explicit coupling blocks and the principal part built in,
trained and graded in the energy pairing, with thin gaps and thin shells
held out; the cheap next nonlearned test is whether a curvature-indexed
basis transfers better than a Fourier-indexed one. Chapter
@sec-boundary-response has the tables; figures
`studies/boundary_response/fig_*.png`.

## 2026-09-09 — Ops: DrivAerML volume filesystem stall; one campaign-A chain blocked by a truncated checkpoint {#sec-nb-ops-stall}

Every lane reading the DrivAerML volume dataset (D1's six, campaign D's
four, the main session's and the density track's interior lanes) stopped
writing logs for about an hour from 13:42; DrivAerML surface and HiLift
lanes were unaffected, so the stall was on that dataset's files, not the
nodes. The chains carry a 3,600 s distributed timeout and resume from their
last checkpoint, so the cost is lost minutes per lane, not results; the
watchers report block markers so that two consecutive links failing with
identical collective-timeout fingerprints are recognised as a stall and
resubmitted, not read as a failure. Separately, campaign A's lane 28
(`campA_hl_transolver_n35_d3_seed43`) blocked because a checkpoint written
during the stall was truncated ("neither a valid zip nor tar archive"); the
file was quarantined under the run's `checkpoints/quarantine/`, the block
marker cleared, and the chain resubmitted (job 692786), resuming from the
previous checkpoint at epoch 11. Campaign A's launch record: 72 chains,
pilots accepted at epoch 100 after one hour, the 210-case rule corrected
before launch because the pool is 180 geometries × 7 angles rather than
126 × 10 (`studies/campaign_a_draws/PREREG.md` carries the correction).

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: C3 — the identifiability floor is real and architecture-independent on an exact paired-condition problem, and a per-point condition input repairs it {#sec-nb-c3-verdict}

The paired-condition control (`studies/paired_conditions/`, preregistered
in its `PREREG.md`; reference and training on a compute node through
`srun --overlap`, since the local host was saturated) built exterior
potential flow on 41 bodies in free air and at 0.6 half-heights above a
ground plane by the image method, qualified against the analytic sphere
(4.4 × 10⁻⁵), with two instrument repairs recorded before training
(collocation at exact surface points along facet-centroid directions with
analytic normals, after a first pass that solved the polyhedron's flow; and
per-case residual and refinement gates at 2 × 10⁻³ and 5 × 10⁻³, amended
from 10⁻³ with the reason in the study notebook; 38 of 41 bodies pass) and
a 3,000-step training length after a 600-step pass proved too weak (the
in-distribution error exceeded the floor). Results on held-out shapes (seed
means, relative L2 of C_p, free air / ground): current encoding trained on
both conditions 0.075 / 0.123; with a per-point ground-proximity scalar
0.045 / 0.058; free-air-only reference 0.040 / 0.157 out of condition;
condition-blind multilayer perceptron 0.237 / 0.219; analytic equal-mixture
floor 0.080 / 0.071. Repair CONFIRMED (1.14x and 1.46x the reference, bar
1.5x; the conditioned model fits its training set at 1.49x). Floor: the
blind model's paired error 0.099 is 1.31x the floor (≥ 0.8x met) and 2.49x
the reference, below the 3x clause, which was miscalibrated (expected
√(0.040² + 0.076²) / 0.040 = 2.15x); recorded as a preregistration
calibration error, not rewritten. Architecture independence holds (the
perceptron at 3.0x the floor). Signature: 78% of the blind model's squared
error on ground cases in the lowest height quarter (57–88%). Chapter
@sec-controls-paired states what this does and does not license about the
DrivAerML → SHIFT-SUV compound shift.

## 2026-09-09 — Ops: the interior-lane stall is a pinned-memory hang in the reader, not I/O; D1 and campaign-D chains held, workaround staged {#sec-nb-ops-pin}

The density track's instrumented probe (stack dumps every ten minutes)
located the stall reported in @sec-nb-ops-stall: on the stuck rank the main
thread waits without timeout in the DataLoader prefetch hand-off
(`physicsnemo/datapipes/protocols.py:366`, via `datapipes/dataloader.py`)
for a prefetch worker that is inside `tensordict.pin_memory()` called from
`DomainMeshReader.__getitem__` (`readers/mesh.py:690`); the other ranks then
spin in the recipe's step-failure barrier, which is what the collective
timeout reports. Every DrivAerML interior lane on the cluster hung this way
from about 12:14; HiLift and DrivAerML surface lanes were unaffected. My
six D1 links restarted from their checkpoints after the first timeout and
deadlocked again within minutes at the same epochs (22 / 22 / 12 / 12 / 22
/ 22), and the four campaign-D lanes before their first checkpoint, which
is the signature of a hang on the first samples rather than a leak. Ten
nodes were therefore burning idle; all ten chains were held (stalled links
cancelled, chain-ahead links on hold). Workaround identified by the main
session: the recipe key `dataloader.pin_memory` (true in `conf/base.yaml`;
read by `datasets.py` and passed to the reader) as the per-lane override
`dataloader.pin_memory=false`, no code change; it is added to
`v0/v0_support_aga.sbatch` and `v0/v0_interior_d_aga.sbatch`, along with
a 1,200 s collective timeout, and the chains will be released when the
probe lane has stepped normally for fifteen minutes. Two records for the
affected lanes: the pinned-to-pageable change costs a few percent per step
at 10,000 + 10,000 tokens (to be measured on the probe lane), so the D1 and
campaign-D step times are not comparable with the reference arm's 0.28 s
without that caveat; and the hand-off's missing timeout is a robustness bug
worth an upstream fix (`Future.result(timeout)` with a named error)
independent of the pinning cause.

**Released (addendum to @sec-nb-ops-pin).** The density track's probe lane
(ISLA query tokens + SDF, density arm, seed 42) resumed from epoch 310 with
`dataloader.pin_memory=false` and stepped normally for more than fifteen
minutes past the point where four consecutive pinned attempts had hung
(epochs 311–312), so the ten held chains were released; eight started at
once, two wait on priority. Measured cost of the workaround on GB300 at
10,000 surface plus 10,000 query tokens: 0.388 s per step against 0.287 s
pinned, a 35% penalty, expected to be similar for GeoTransolver-volume.
From this date every interior step time in this program is quoted as a
pin_memory=false number, and the D1 and campaign-D cost readouts are
compared with the reference arm's step time only after the same penalty is
applied to it (or the reference is re-measured under the same setting); the
root cause of the hang inside `TensorDict.pin_memory` in the reader's
prefetch thread stays open.

## 2026-09-09 — Ops: the released links still carried pinned memory and hung again at 17:34; nine cancelled, chain-ahead links carry the workaround {#sec-nb-ops-recancel}

Releasing a held Slurm job does not re-read its batch script. The ten
interior chains released in the addendum to @sec-nb-ops-pin therefore
started their held links with the original script (`pin_memory: true` in
each run's printed configuration, collective timeout 3,600 s), while only
the links submitted after the edit carry `dataloader.pin_memory=false`.
Nine of the ten held links stepped normally for about 35 minutes (D1
support-12 arms to epochs 42–43, support-4 to 44–45, passive-12 to 35, the
hidden-344 query-token carrier to 31, GeoTransolver-volume without local
features to 33–35) and then all stopped logging within the same minute,
17:33–17:34, and stayed silent for 40 minutes; the one link that had
already rolled over to a post-edit script (hidden-344 carrier, seed 42,
`pin_memory: false`) kept stepping at 0.48–0.51 s. The synchronized onset
across nine nodes says the trigger is a shared event (a Lustre or fabric
hiccup) that the pinned-memory hand-off cannot recover from, while the
unpinned reader rides through it; that is consistent with the stack dumps
in @sec-nb-ops-pin. It is not strictly cluster-wide: the main session
reports that its two pinned interior links on the same cluster kept
stepping through 17:34, so the hang is intermittent and pinned links are
exposed to it while no unpinned link has shown it yet. At 18:14 the nine stalled links were cancelled so their
successors (all verified to contain the override and the 1,200 s timeout)
start at once; each chain link resubmits its successor, so no top-up is
needed. Cost: one partial epoch per lane (checkpoints are per epoch) plus
the 40 idle minutes on nine nodes. Lesson for the ops record: after editing
a chain's script, cancel-and-resubmit the held links rather than releasing
them.

## 2026-09-09 — Protocol: D1 and campaign D compare only with references re-evaluated under the same code snapshot; re-evaluation launched {#sec-nb-evalpoints}

The main session reports that one checkpoint re-evaluated under the newly
merged code plus a recipe copy scored 6.1% differently from its
training-time evaluation, and that every frozen cluster snapshot used by
the program book (`code`, `code_isla2`–`code_isla5`) produces bit-identical
sampled validation points, which is why the book's comparisons stand. The
D1 and campaign-D lanes run from a new snapshot (`code_support` plus
`recipe_support`), so their numbers may not be compared with the reference
values recorded in @sec-nb-d1-launch (ISLA query tokens + SDF 0.0567 /
0.0853 / 0.1215; GeoTransolver-volume 0.0620 / 0.1334 / 0.0939) until the
sampled points are shown identical. Two checks, preregistered here before
any D1 evaluation exists: (1) the four reference checkpoints
(`v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed{42,43}`, `v0_gt_vol_seed{42,43}`) are re-evaluated
under `code_support` + `recipe_support` on the 48 validation cars (job
695764, launcher `v0/v0_ref_reeval_aga.sbatch`, outputs
`$T/v0_evals_support/`, originals untouched); if their 48-car means match
the recorded values to three decimals and the per-car interior points are
`allclose` to the originals, the recorded references stand, otherwise the
re-evaluated values become the references for every D1 and campaign-D
comparison and the grading script is pointed at them. (2) Because the
support transform moves the first 5,000 points of the reader's
deterministic per-case sample into the support set, the 5,000 points each
D1 arm is scored on must be a subset of the reference's 10,000-point sample
for the same car; this is checked on the saved prediction artifacts for a
few cars once the first D1 evaluation exists. A per-point relative L2 over
a random half of the same sample is comparable with the full-sample value
up to sampling noise, which the two-seed spread already exceeds.

## 2026-09-09 — Ops: the interior stall recurred at 19:22 with pinned memory off; pinning was a site, not the cause {#sec-nb-ops-stall3}

Third synchronized stall of the day. Every DrivAerML interior lane on the
cluster, mine (six D1, four campaign-D) and the main session's (density and
neighbour arms, ISLA query-token seed 44), stopped logging between 19:22 and
19:25, all running with `dataloader.pin_memory=false`; one D1 lane
(support-12, seed 42) followed at 19:32. At the same minutes every surface
and HiLift lane on the cluster (campaigns A, B and C, the scaling study, the
main session's seven unit-drive DrivAerML surface lanes, which finished and
evaluated normally) kept stepping, and a login-node directory listing on the
same Lustre file system returned in 90 ms. The reading of @sec-nb-ops-pin,
that pinned memory is the cause, is therefore superseded. The main session's
latest stack dumps place the stuck rank inside the host-to-device copy of
the loaded sample (`TensorDict.to(device)` from `domain_mesh.py`), with the
other ranks waiting in the step barrier: one rank's CUDA context stops
completing host-side operations, and pinning was merely where it first
showed. Two facts constrain the cause: it is interior-only (the volume
lanes are the only ones moving 10,000-point interior arrays per sample,
with the largest host-to-device traffic), and the onset is synchronized
across about fifteen nodes and two sessions (17:34, 19:22), which argues
for a shared trigger rather than per-node driver state. Neither is fixable
in user space; the main session is surfacing the driver-side question to
Peter for the cluster team. Mitigation both sessions converge on: a short
collective timeout so the ranks die instead of idling (my launchers go from
1,200 s to 600 s for future links; the ranks reported NCCL timeouts at
19:42–19:45 and the links exit and restart from the last epoch checkpoint)
plus link recycling on a 15-minute idle log. Each stall costs one timeout
plus one partial epoch per lane; at roughly one stall per 30–60 minutes per
lane this is a 10–25% throughput loss on the interior campaigns, tolerable,
and the reader hand-off's bounded wait remains a robustness fix worth
carrying upstream independently.

## 2026-09-09 — Campaign E, bf16 preview: only the similarity-gauge ISLA survives the 10:1 density bias; every input-matched baseline and both other ISLA configurations collapse; float32 rerun launched under the new reporting rule {#sec-nb-campe-bf16}

**Protocol change first.** The main session's snapshot ladder found that
the same checkpoint scores 0.0568 in float32 inference and 0.0588 or
0.0624 under two different bf16 graphs (per car up to 31%), so bf16
evaluation is not a stable instrument; float32 inference is now the
reporting instrument for every comparative number in both programs (CLAIMS
rule 31a069280, notebook #sec-nb-fp32-instrument in the program book), and
bf16 numbers are kept only for a per-architecture offset table. Applied
here: the campaign A eval launcher writes float32 to `hl_evals_fp32/` (its
first five bf16 evaluations stay for the offset table and are redone in
float32); the campaign B, D1 and campaign-D eval launchers evaluate each
run in float32 (`*_evals_fp32/`) and bf16 side by side; D1 and campaign D
will compare only with float32 references (`$T/v0_evals_fp32/`, main
session), not with the bf16 0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215 and 0.0620 / 0.1334 /
0.0939, so the same-snapshot identity of @sec-nb-evalpoints-verdict is a
bf16 statement and will be repeated in float32. The bf16 numbers below are
therefore a preview; the float32 rerun of all eleven campaign-E runs is job
696011 (`transfer/campaign_e_density_fp32_aga.sbatch`, outputs
`$T/transfer/campaign_e_fp32/`).

**Setting.** The density probe (@sec-nb-campe-launch) scores each
checkpoint on the 48 DrivAerML validation cars twice: on a uniform draw of
10,000 cells through the same two-stage 40,000 → 10,000 pipeline, and on a
Poisson-biased draw whose inclusion probability is ten times higher on the
front half of the car than on the back (exact Horvitz–Thompson weights,
937 to 9,366 per cell, total measure preserved within 3%, centroid of the
sample shifted 0.2 body lengths forward). The similarity-gauge ISLA's
factor of 1.20 is the program book's density-robustness claim; the probe
had never been run on an input-matched baseline.

**Readout (bf16, 48 cars, pressure relative L2; factor = biased ÷ uniform).**

| arm | seeds | uniform | biased | factor (per seed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver, unit drive (`uw_gt_unit_lr1e3`) | 3 | 0.0554 | 0.480 | 8.7 (10.8, 7.2, 8.1) |
| Transolver, unit drive, lr 3e-3 (`uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3`) | 2 | 0.0561 | 0.201 | 3.6 (2.1, 5.1) |
| ISLA reference, constant gauge (`iw_mt2_lr1e3`) | 2 | 0.0579 | 0.675 | 11.6 (12.0, 11.3) |
| ISLA similarity gauge (`iw_mt2_gauge`) | 2 | 0.0633 | 0.0762 | 1.203 (1.204, 1.202) |
| ISLA weights off (`now_mt2_lr1e3`) | 2 | 0.0566 | 1.041 | 18.3 (22.0, 14.7) |

: Every car is worse under the bias for every run of the first three arms and the weights-off arm; the gauge arm is worse on 44 and 46 of 48 cars. Artifact `$T/transfer/campaign_e/campaign_e_density.json` (reducer `studies/campaign_e_evalonly/reduce_campaign_e.py`). {#tbl-campe-bf16}

**Instrument checks.** The gauge pair under this launcher reproduces the
book's 0.063 / 0.076 (factor 1.203 against 1.20), and the constant-gauge
ISLA at 11.6 sits in the book's recorded 13–14.5 band within seed
variation, so the probe behaves as it did on 2026-09-02; the biased
artifacts have the expected cell counts (9,969–10,094) and weights.

**Reading, pending float32.** The preregistered "holds" clause named the
ISLA reference configuration and required its factor ≤ 1.24; that
configuration degrades 11.6x, so the clause is unmet by construction, a
miscalibration recorded rather than rewritten: the book's 1.20 belongs to
the gauge arm alone. Graded with the gauge arm as "ISLA", the claim holds
by a wide margin: the input-matched unit-drive GeoTransolver degrades 8.7x
(against 3.6x for the physical-drive GeoTransolver recorded in the book;
a different trained model, so no contradiction, but the unit drive makes
GeoTransolver less density-robust), Transolver 3.6x, and the two other ISLA
configurations are the least robust of all, weights-off reaching an error
above 1.0 (worse than predicting zero). Mechanism, stated as a hypothesis
for the float32 verdict: the similarity gauge normalizes ISLA's kernel by
the local measure so the HT weights are consumed correctly, whereas the
constant-gauge ISLA's measure-weighted sums see a ten-fold weight range
they were never trained on, the weights-off ISLA has no measure to correct
the density at all, and GeoTransolver's radius-based local features are
density statistics by construction. For the NOW-L decision (weights off as
the best fair configuration) this is the cost side: weights off buys 2.8%
on DrivAerML and loses all density robustness. Verdict and chapter text
after job 696011.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict, campaign E density probe (float32): the similarity gauge is the only density-robust configuration (1.21x); unit-drive GeoTransolver 9.5x, Transolver 3.9x, constant-gauge ISLA 12.1x, weights-off ISLA 19.1x {#sec-nb-campe-verdict}

**Readout (float32 inference, the reporting instrument; 48 DrivAerML
validation cars; pressure relative L2; factor = biased ÷ uniform).**

| arm | seeds | uniform | biased | factor (per seed) | bf16 uniform, for the offset table |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver, unit drive | 3 | 0.0505 | 0.479 | 9.5 (11.8, 7.9, 8.8) | 0.0554 (+9.7%) |
| Transolver, unit drive, lr 3e-3 | 2 | 0.0517 | 0.200 | 3.9 (2.2, 5.5) | 0.0561 (+8.5%) |
| ISLA reference, constant gauge | 2 | 0.0558 | 0.675 | 12.1 (12.5, 11.7) | 0.0579 (+3.8%) |
| ISLA similarity gauge | 2 | 0.0616 | 0.0746 | 1.21 (1.21, 1.21) | 0.0633 (+2.8%) |
| ISLA weights off | 2 | 0.0544 | 1.043 | 19.1 (23.1, 15.2) | 0.0566 (+4.0%) |

: Every car is worse under the bias for every run except the gauge arm's (47 and 46 of 48). Artifacts `studies/campaign_e_evalonly/campaign_e_density_fp32_2026-09-09.json` (float32) and `campaign_e_density_bf16_2026-09-09.json` (bf16 preview, @tbl-campe-bf16); reducer `reduce_campaign_e.py`. {#tbl-campe-fp32}

**Verdict.** By the letter of the preregistration the outcome is *between*,
because the "holds" clause named the ISLA reference configuration, whose
factor is 12.1; that clause could not have been met and is recorded as a
miscalibration (the book's 1.20 belongs to the similarity-gauge arm, which
this protocol reproduces at 1.21). Graded with the gauge arm as ISLA, the
claim **holds by a wide margin**: the input-matched unit-drive
GeoTransolver degrades 9.5x (its factor exceeds the 1.32 bar by a factor of
seven), Transolver 3.9x, and the gauge's 1.21 is inside the 1.24 bar. The
absolute levels are reported with the factors: the gauge arm pays 10–20% on
the uniform draw for its robustness (0.0616 against 0.0505 for
GeoTransolver and 0.0558 for the constant-gauge ISLA), so the trade is a
fifth of the accuracy on well-sampled surfaces for an eight- to fifteen-fold
smaller error under a ten-fold density skew. The two non-gauge ISLA
configurations are the least robust of all five, and weights-off (the
program's best fair configuration on canonical data, 2.8% ahead of weights
on) has no measure to correct the density and reaches an error above 1.0,
worse than predicting zero; that is the cost side of the weights-off
decision, as the main session anticipated.

**Mechanism, as far as this readout supports it.** The biased draw carries
exact Horvitz–Thompson weights (ten-fold range) in the measure field. The
similarity gauge normalizes ISLA's kernel by the local measure, so those
weights are consumed as a quadrature correction and the field is
reconstructed from the sparse half almost as well as from the dense half;
the constant-gauge ISLA sees weights outside its training range in every
measure-weighted sum; the weights-off ISLA discards them and sees the
front-heavy token cloud as geometry; GeoTransolver's radius-based local
features are neighbour-count statistics that shift ten-fold with density;
Transolver's slice attention degrades more gracefully (2.2–5.5x) because
its routing is by learned features rather than by counts. These are
readings consistent with the numbers, not separately tested.

**Instrument note.** The float32 uniform levels are 8.5–9.7% below the
bf16 ones for GeoTransolver and Transolver but only 2.8–4.0% for the three
ISLA configurations, so bf16 evaluation has been penalizing the baselines
more than ISLA in every bf16 comparison of this program; a per-architecture
offset that the main session's offset table now has five more entries for.

**What changes.** The program book's density-robustness paragraph gains a
fair comparison and survives, with the gauge named as the mechanism and its
10–20% uniform-draw cost stated; the weights-off configuration is
recommended for canonical benchmarks only. Next: no further node time on
this question; the mechanism reading would be tested by a gauge arm with
weights off (does the gauge alone suffice?) if the program wants it.
